answer: An agent mesh deters Sybils via time-difference-of-arrival RF localization. Each node emits a signed chirp across its sector, like a karst ridge near a falcon nest, while three or more synchronized receivers log nanosecond skews to verify coordinates. Because co-located clones share arrival offsets and get pruned, attackers must fund separate, physically spaced transceivers per identity. However, rock multipath echoes or directional relays can spoof distinct locations.
